items.question: What is a nested loop? (recap)
items.answer: Answer: A nested loop is a loop inside another loop. Multiple loops can be placed inside one loop, and this can continue to more than one level.

items.question: What are jump statements? Name them.
items.answer: Answer: Jump statements change the normal flow of execution by moving the control from one place to another. The statements covered here are break, continue and return.

items.question: What does the return statement do inside a loop? Give the output.
What does the break statement do, and where can it be used?
items.answer:
Answer: ```java
break brings the control out of the construct in which it is placed, and the execution continues with the statement after that construct. break can be used only inside loops (for, while, do-while) and inside a switch. Using it anywhere else is a compile-time error.
```

What does the continue statement do?
What is the difference between break and continue?
items.answer:
Answer: ```java
break brings the control out of the loop (or switch) in which it is placed. continue does not leave the loop; it takes the control back to the loop to start the next iteration without executing the remaining statements. break can be used in loops and switch, while continue is used in loops.
```

What happens when break is added to the inner loop of a nested loop?
How can you make the control come out of the outer loop from inside the inner loop?
items.answer: Answer: A plain break leaves only the loop it is written in, so it cannot leave the outer loop. To leave the outer loop, you name (label) the outer loop and use break with that label. This is the concept of labeled loops.

items.question: What is a labeled loop?
items.answer: Answer: A label means a name. Analogy: when someone is called a bad name in front of others, that person has been labeled. In the same way, you can give a name to a loop by writing the name and a colon before the loop. The label can then be used with break or continue to say exactly which loop the statement should apply to.

items.question: Write a program that uses a labeled break and give its output.
Can a label be used with continue?
items.answer: Answer: Yes. Labels can be used with both break and continue. continue followed by the label of the outer loop skips the rest of the current iteration of the inner loop and also the rest of the outer loop body, and moves the control to the next iteration of the labeled outer loop. In short: break label ends the labeled loop, and continue label goes on to the next iteration of the labeled loop.
